title: Rabbi Yehuda bar Zevida
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Berakhot 63b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.63b.24): What was the blessing with which Oved Edom was blessed? That they bore six at one birth. And in [Bava Batra 120a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.120a.2-3): he said, This teaches that she developed the signs of maturity; this teaches that he performed an act of marriage with her. So too it should read in [Sotah 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.12a.15). And in Sotah, chapter 4, halakhah 4 as supplied: Rabbi Yuda bar Zevida said, “Yehosef” is written in full.[^4] And in [Berakhot 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.12b.14): Rabbi Abbahu bar Zutrati said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda bar Zevida: They sought to fix the portion of Balak in the Shema, and why did they not fix it? Because of the burden on the public.

And in [Yerushalmi Berakhot 1:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.1.5.5), Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said this statement in his name, and there he is called Rabbi Yehuda bar Zevoda. From this Hyman infers that he was a native of the Land of Israel, and proposes reading "Rabbi Yehuda bar Zevida" throughout.

We find that he had two brothers. Rabbi Abba, as in [Yevamot 83b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.83b.9): Rabbi Abba, brother of Rabbi Yehuda bar Zavdi, said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda, who said in the name of Rav. And in Kiddushin 43b it reads: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rabbi Abba, who said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda bar Zavdi in the name of Rav; Hyman proposes reading it as in Yevamot. And Rabbi Simon is his brother, as in [Yerushalmi Bava Batra 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bava_Batra.3.1.4).[^3]

notes.text: The body explicitly says he was from the Land of Israel (בר א״י), and Hyman consequently proposes Rabbi rather than the heading’s Rav throughout. His chronology, sibling relationships and proposed transmission-chain correction remain his conclusions.

The inspected Berakhot 63b names Rav Yehudah bar Zevida and specifies a mother-in-law and eight daughters-in-law each bearing six at one birth. Hyman’s shorter plural wording is preserved without adding one wife. His Land-of-Israel, Rabbi-title, sibling and transmission-chain conclusions remain his; the proposed cross-locus identifications are not newly admitted.

Berakhot specifies that a mother-in-law and eight daughters-in-law each bore six at one birth. Sotah 12a attributes the signs-of-maturity interpretation to plain Rabbi Yehudah. Yerushalmi Berakhot gives Shmuel bar Nachman in the name of Yehudah bar Zevoda. Yerushalmi Bava Batra names Simon his brother and gives Rav as the authority. Heilprin collects these family and transmission notices. See [Heilprin’s corresponding entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1680&lang=en).

The discussion appears in [Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 7:4:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.7.4.9), where Rabbi Yehuda bar Zevida cites Psalm 81:6 for the spelling “Yehosef” when counting the letters on the stones of the ephod. The supplied locator gives chapter 4.
